turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Ah, one second, this screen has gone blank again. Ok. I am with you, please go on.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Good afternoon, doctor. I hope I am not disturbing you. My partner wished me to show you a mole on my back.
[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Sorry, the parking was quite mad outside. Doctor, the colour has changed. It was light brown only, and now one side is much darker.
[SEG0004] person_1 (DOCTOR): Hmm, the mouse is stuck. Say that once more? The colour?
[SEG0005] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The colour, yes. Darker, with a blackish area on one edge. I have been watching it for some time.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): And, uh, it bled once, doctor. Roughly a month back, when the shirt was rubbing on it. Only a few drops, and then it stopped by itself.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Is it painful? Any itching?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): In college I used to get very bad sunburn, doctor, on the shoulders and the back, every summer. We were playing cricket in the afternoon and we never put any cream.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Mm. The sunburn I will note. But I asked about pain and itching. Is the mole painful? Does it itch?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): I apologise, doctor. No pain, and it does not itch.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right. How long has the mole been there? When did you first notice it?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm. The mole itself has been there for years, I believe. The change, she noticed it maybe three months back. I cannot give the exact date, I am sorry.
[SEG0013] person_4 (NURSE): Excuse me, doctor. Weight today is seventy eight kilograms. And the repeat list has telmisarten 40 milligrams every morning.
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): The weight is correct, madam. But kindly note, the telmisartan is twenty milligrams, not forty. My physician reduced it last year.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Err, I only half heard that, this fan is loud. Any drug reaction before? Any medicine you cannot take?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): I am not certain, doctor. Maybe the antibiotic or the painkiller. I had swelling of the lips on one occasion, but nobody told me which of the two it was.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Family side, quickly. Diabetes, pressure, any skin cancer?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): My father had diabetes in his fifties, my mother did not, and another sister has pressure but no sugar. Nobody in the family has had skin cancer, to my knowledge.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Work and daily habits, please. This referral form keeps jumping and I am losing my place.

[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): I am an accounts officer in a garment export firm, and I work nearly eleven hours a day, six days a week. My diet is simple home food, mostly vegetarian, rice and dal. I walk twenty minutes in the morning before office. Alcohol only during festivals, one small peg, not otherwise.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Shirt up, please, let me see the back. One moment, the lamp is not... ok, there.

[SEG0022] person_1 (DOCTOR): On the left upper back there is a mole, roughly 8 millimetres across. It is asymmetrical, the border is irregular, and the colour is uneven, brown with a black area at one edge. I do not see an ulcer, and it is not bleeding now.
[SEG0023] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): That black part was definitely not there last year. I keep telling him, but he is busy only.
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Please be frank with me, doctor. Is this a serious matter?
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): I cannot confirm it just by looking. My working impression is an atypical mole, and I cannot rule out a melanoma, so a skin specialist should see it.
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): I am referring you to dermatology, and they should see you within two weeks. Do not scratch it, and please use a sun cream when you go out.
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you, doctor. Should I stop the telmisartan in the meantime?
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): No, please continue it as you take it now. I am not adding any new medicine. If it bleeds again before the appointment, come back sooner.
[SEG0029] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I will bring him, doctor. Otherwise he will say the office cannot manage without him.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): I am grateful for your time, doctor. We will follow what you have said.

spec.situation: Person with a mole on the back that partner says has changed in colour; bleeding once; sunburn history; doctor describes the mole by features and plans a dermatology referral.

traps.happens: The doctor asks about drug reactions. Variants (use ONE per encounter): (a) the patient says 'No, never, I have taken penicillin and everything' (no allergy); (b) the patient is unsure ('maybe the antibiotic or the painkiller, nobody told me which'); (c) a real allergy with the reaction described; (d) allergies are never asked.
traps.label_rule: (a) NO allergy entry: negative_findings 'Allergies' absent. (b) allergy with status uncertain, the substance as described, the reaction if said, plus an allergy_uncertain uncertainty. (c) allergy with the reaction. (d) nothing at all. NEVER list a medicine the patient has taken without a reaction as an allergy, and the plan must not prescribe a drug of a recorded allergy's family.

traps.happens: In ONE long answer the patient lists several relatives and their conditions ('my father had diabetes in his fifties, mother did not, another sister has pressure but no sugar'), and in another long answer their job, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol.
traps.label_rule: Every relative with a stated condition is a separate family_history entry (relative, condition). Relatives said NOT to have a condition are not family_history entries. Occupation, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol/tobacco each become social_history entries as said (no inventions). Nothing from the doctor's questions is a fact.

features: patient_answers_other_question: the patient answers a different question than the one asked, and the doctor repeats or lets it go.
disputed_numbers: the nurse reads a value and the patient or relative disagrees or remembers another (a dose, a weight, a BP). Keep both and record an uncertainty.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

bad.reason: Back mole present for years is supported; certainty 'certain' is not, patient says 'I believe'.
bad.text: Back mole (category=dermatological, status=present, duration=several years, temporality=current, body_site=back, reported_by=patient, certainty=certain)

omissions.text: Current telmisartan dose is 20 mg every morning; recorded medication entry lacks the dose and the transcript explicitly corrects the nurse's 40 mg list entry.
Patient said the telmisartan dose had been reduced last year by his physician.
Family member described the mole colour change more specifically as a blackish area on one edge, and said it was definitely not there last year.
The prior bleeding episode stopped by itself after a few drops.
Family history also included that the mother did not have diabetes.
Doctor advised to continue telmisartan as currently taken and stated no new medicine was being added.
